questions.q: What does the term "guestology" refer to in Disney's service model?
a: Studying guests to understand their expectations
Training staff on safety protocols
Designing park attractions
Marketing Disney merchandise
questions.why: The summary says guestology is the science of getting to know customers and discovering what they expect.

questions.q: Which quality‑standard component would make a cast member pause a show for a lost child?
a: Safety
Courtesy
Show
Efficiency

questions.q: How does Disney demonstrate the "setting" delivery system in its hotel dining rooms?
a: Using themed doorknobs like those from Alice in Wonderland
Offering free Wi‑Fi to all guests
Playing live music during meals
Providing complimentary snacks
questions.why: The summary cites identical themed doorknobs as an example of setting reflecting Disney values.

questions.q: In the integration point, how is the factor of courtesy evaluated?
a: By checking how employees, environment and processes each support it
By measuring guest wait times only
By counting the number of staff uniforms
By tracking merchandise sales
questions.why: Integration looks at how employees, setting, and processes contribute to courtesy.

questions.q: What insight did Disney gain from surveys about Brazilian visitors?
a: They liked singing in large groups, prompting Portuguese‑speaking staff training
They preferred quiet rides, leading to fewer loud attractions
They visited only on weekends, so staffing was reduced
They wanted more fast‑food options, so new restaurants opened
questions.why: Surveys showed Brazilian guests sang in groups, so Disney trained Portuguese‑speaking employees.
